symptom: document.modelContext undefined on localhost and example.com even though agent-browser already enables WebMCPTesting/DevToolsWebMCPSupport; WebMCP tools only appeared on an origin-trial demo page. `--enable-blink-features=WebMCP,WebMCPTesting,DocumentModelcontext` (comma list) crashed Chrome headless with "Multiple targets are not supported in headless mode".
cause: agent-browser passes --enable-features=WebMCPTesting,DevToolsWebMCPSupport by default, but that content feature alone does not expose document.modelContext. The gate that actually exposes it is the content feature `WebMCP` (the origin trial feature name; the googlechromelabs demos enable it per-origin via a <meta http-equiv="origin-trial"> token with feature "WebMCP"). Also navigator.modelContext no longer exists in Chrome 156/157; the API is document.modelContext.
fix: Launch a fresh managed browser with: agent_browser({args:["--args","--enable-features=WebMCP","open","<url>"], sessionMode:"fresh"}). Then `webmcp list` / `webmcp invoke <tool> --params '{...}'` work on any localhost/file page that registers tools. Verify in-page via typeof document.modelContext.
verify: agent_browser eval: (() => typeof document.modelContext)() === "object" on http://127.0.0.1:8787/, then `webmcp list` returns the locally registered tools.
